<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reviewing existing files including CommentResponse, tickets.openapi.yaml, and frontend API code to prepare for implementing phases 5 through 8.

Evaluating patterns to distinguish omitted properties from explicit JSON nulls in UpdateTicketRequest. Considering Optional fields, Map-based structures, or field tracking classes to handle partial updates correctly.

Realized that @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL) cannot distinguish omitted properties from explicit JSON nulls, since both deserialize as Java null. This means the current approach may not satisfy the requirement to reject explicit nulls while allowing omitted fields to remain unset.

Reconsidered the null handling approach. Since explicit JSON nulls fail during deserialization while omitted properties become Java null, null values in the service layer naturally mean "leave this field unchanged." This resolves the ambiguity between omitted and explicit nulls. Now designing the UpdateTicketRequest record structure.

Finalized the UpdateTicketRequest record with five fields. Title, description, assignee, and resolution notes each carry @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL) and size constraints. Priority also uses the same null-failure setter.

Added a compact constructor to the UpdateTicketRequest record that trims string fields and leaves null values untouched. Blank values for present fields will trigger a 400 error via @AssertTrue or a custom validator.

Considering @AssertTrue for blank-field validation, but realized it would not map errors to the correct fields. Field-level validation is needed instead.

Evaluating a `@Pattern` regex validator to catch blank strings without relying on `@AssertTrue`. Also considering a custom class-level validator or controller-side validation as alternatives to the record compact constructor.

Ruled out `@NotBlank` because it rejects null values, which would break optional fields in the update request. A custom validator is the only viable path forward.

Service-layer validation is ruled out because tests verify no interactions with the service. A custom `@InitBinder` or `ConstraintValidator` is being considered. A dedicated `@ValidUpdateTicket` annotation with a custom validator is another option. The compact constructor approach was rejected since it would not produce standard field-level errors.

Settled on a custom class-level validator for the UpdateTicketRequest record. Standard annotations like @NotEmpty and @Length still fail on null, so a dedicated constraint is required. The validator will be applied directly to the record type to ensure validation occurs at the @Valid level.

Drafted the `@ValidUpdateTicket` annotation and its `UpdateTicketRequestValidator` implementation. The validator checks each non-null field for blank values and adds property-level constraint violations mapped to the corresponding record fields.

Clarified that priority is an enum, so a blank priority likely means an invalid enum value rather than a blank string. For Phase 7, planning TicketSummary and TicketPage DTOs, an ILIKE repository query, and a GET /api/tickets endpoint with pagination validation. The controller must return 400 when page is provided without size.

Defined exact 400 validation rules for Phase 7 pagination and filtering: size must be between 1 and 100, page must be zero or greater, and status must be a valid enum value. These validations will run in the controller before any service call. For the ticket search query, drafted a native SQL JPA @Query using ILIKE with escaped LIKE wildcards on title and description.

Native SQL LIKE escaping is tricky in JPQL. A Java helper will escape backslashes, percent signs, and underscores before passing the pattern to PostgreSQL ILIKE. Criteria API or Specification is also under consideration. Next step is reviewing the OpenAPI contract for response shapes.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Jackson deserializes partial JSON updates into UpdateTicketRequest with null fields. This causes ticket edits to fail silently.

The `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)` annotation only rejects explicit JSON nulls, not omitted fields. Jackson appears to deserialize missing properties as null anyway, which explains why the validation error still fires.

The task explicitly requires omitted properties to become Java null. `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)` is incorrectly rejecting them. Only explicit JSON nulls should fail.

A different strategy is needed. `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)` likely rejects both omitted and explicit nulls. Alternatives include Optional fields, JsonNode tracking, or a custom deserializer. A standard Spring PATCH pattern with `@JsonIgnoreProperties` and `@Nullable` is being considered.

The task explicitly requires `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)`, so the PATCH pattern with `@Nullable` is not viable. A custom `JsonDeserializer` using `JsonNode` could detect whether a property was omitted or explicitly set to null. Alternatively, `@JsonMerge` or an `Optional` wrapper might work.

A custom `JsonDeserializer` is being considered to explicitly reject JSON nulls while allowing omitted fields to deserialize as Java null. The `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)` behavior for omitted properties on records is also being verified.

Jackson documentation confirms `Nulls.FAIL` throws on null values. Missing properties in record deserialization appear to be treated as null, so the annotation rejects omitted fields too. A custom deserializer or a mutable class with `@JsonAnySetter` is now the preferred path. Using `JsonNode` directly in the controller was dismissed as too invasive.

The chosen fix is to replace the record with a mutable class. Omitted properties in a mutable class remain as Java null without triggering `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)`, since Jackson skips the setter entirely when the property is absent. Records behave differently because the deserializer passes null to the constructor for missing fields.

The concrete implementation is now clear. UpdateTicketRequest will be rewritten as a mutable class with private fields and getters. This ensures omitted properties remain Java null, while explicit JSON nulls correctly trigger the @JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL) validation.

The mutable class will use record-style accessor methods such as `title()` to match the existing service API. Setters will trim strings and rely on `@JsonSetter(nulls = Nulls.FAIL)` to catch explicit JSON nulls before the setter runs. Omitted properties will leave fields as null because Jackson skips the setter entirely.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Phase 6 passed. Committed and moving to Phase 7.

Phase 7 covers listing and searching tickets. Tasks include validation tests, DTOs, repository and service logic with ILIKE search, a controller endpoint, and frontend UI. Controller validation will reject invalid page, size, and status values.

Spring will resolve the GET /api/tickets route against the existing `/{ticketId}` mapping. The repository search will use a native query with PostgreSQL ILIKE, casting status to varchar and escaping backslashes in the title pattern.

The repository search will match both title and description via ILIKE, ordered by creation date and ticket number descending. A service helper will escape wildcards and trim the search query before building the SQL pattern.

The service method will accept query text, status, page, and size. Missing pagination parameters default to page zero and size equal to total matches. The search pattern is built by trimming the query and escaping wildcards before passing it to the repository.

The service will return a full-page TicketPage when pagination is omitted. When pagination is provided, it will use PageRequest with a sort order. The repository may use JpaSpecificationExecutor for flexible filtering instead of a custom native query.

The repository now extends JpaSpecificationExecutor. A static Specification builder applies the status filter and lowercases title and description for case-insensitive matching.

The specification builder now applies the search pattern with Hibernate's `cb.like` using an escaped backslash. Results are ordered by `createdAt` descending, then `ticketNumber` descending. `TicketSummary` and `TicketPage` records are also being defined.

The controller will validate query parameters directly in the `listTickets` handler. If `page` is provided without `size`, it throws a `BadListRequestException`. A custom exception or `ProblemDetail` will be used for these errors.

An `InvalidListQueryException` will be added for invalid list queries. An `ApiExceptionHandler` will map it to a 400 `ProblemDetail` response.

Tests T047 will cover invalid list query cases in TicketValidationTest using mockMvc. These include requests with page but no size, size outside bounds, negative page, and invalid status. The controller will validate page and size before the service layer. Starting Phase 7 implementation.
</details></think>
